# Alliances and collective security (`collective_security_alliances`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/military.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Warfare, security & deterrence (`military`)
- Deps: helped by international_law_sovereignty, balance_of_power, deterrence, representative_government
- Core idea: An alliance is a promise of mutual aid against an outside enemy; collective security is a promise by all members of a system to act together against any member that breaks the peace. Both let weak states pool strength and deter attack, and both stand or fall with the belief that the promise will be kept. Promises are made binding by precise terms (who must do what, when), by standing shared forces and staffs, hostages or stationed troops, regular congresses, and the knowledge that a defaulter will find no allies later.
- Pitfalls:
  - Free-riding: each member hopes the others will pay and fight, so common leagues act late or not at all (League of Nations, 1931 and 1935)
  - Every ally fears both being abandoned and being dragged into the partner's quarrel
  - The leader turns the league into an empire, as Athens did with the Delian League
  - A rule of unanimity lets one member, usually the aggressor's friend, block action
  - Coalitions break up at the moment of victory when the common enemy is gone
- History: mesopotamia: c. 1259 BC – Egyptian-Hittite treaty of peace and mutual defence; china: 7th–6th c. BC – sworn covenants (meng) of states under a hegemon; 546 BC – Xiang Xu's peace conference of the major states; greece: 6th c. BC – Peloponnesian League; 478 BC – Delian League; 386 BC – first Common Peace (King's Peace); 337 BC – League of Corinth; rome: 493 BC (traditional) – treaty with the Latin League; by 50 BC a web of unequal treaties with allies and client kings; americas: date disputed (12th–16th c.) – Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) confederacy under the Great Law of Peace; 1428 – Aztec Triple Alliance; europe: 1454–1455 – Italian League, 25-year mutual guarantee; 1683 – treaty between Emperor Leopold I and John III Sobieski brings the Polish army to the relief of Vienna; 1684 – Holy League; 1815 – Quadruple Alliance and congress system; global: 1920 – League of Nations; 1945 – United Nations Charter, chapter VII; 1949 – North Atlantic Treaty, article 5
